title: Money Worries Affect Two-Thirds of UK Workers
paragraphs: Money problems are making life hard for many workers in the UK, and they are also affecting their work.

According to research by the company Hymans Robertson, two-thirds of employees in the UK say that worries about money are hurting their productivity at work. This is a big increase. In a similar survey the year before, the number was just 38%.

Other surveys show similar problems. A survey for Stream, a company that offers financial services to workers, asked 2,000 UK employees about money and work. Nearly two-thirds said they worry every month about paying their rent or mortgage. And one in five workers under 35 said they worry every day about paying for basic things.

These worries are affecting people at work. In the Stream survey, 59% said money problems make them feel less energy and less excited about their work. In addition, 83% said they had taken at least one day off in the past year because of stress, worry or illness connected to money.

Many of these workers would like help from their employers. Almost half said they would like better tools to manage their money. Almost half also said they would think about leaving their job for one with better financial benefits.

Peter Briffett, the CEO of Stream, said the UK is a nation under serious financial stress. Briffett also said employers have an important role to play in helping workers feel less worried about money.
